passages.original: Attestantur buic eximiae doctrinae sancti antiqui Patres doctores, defensoresque Ecclesiae, Hilarius, Ambrosius, Augustinus, Gregorius Nazianzenus : hi omnes testimonium tibi praebent, sicut apostolis praebuerunt prophetae.Hilarius sanctus dicit, exponens ver- ba Apostoli doctoris gentium. Ita etenim quæ propriae disciplinae et morum sunt, ad sacerdoti i merilum utilia esse significat. si etiam haec quæ ad docendæ ac tenendae Mei scienliam necessaria sunt, inter reliqua non deerunt : quia non statim boni atque utilis sacerdotis est, aut tantummodo scienter [Ms. Tolet., innocenter] agere , aut tantummodo scienter praedicare;
passages.english: The holy ancient Fathers, teachers and defenders of the Church, bear witness to this excellent teaching: Hilary, Ambrose, Augustine, Gregory Nazianzen. All these offer testimony to you, just as the prophets offered it to the apostles. Saint Hilary says, expounding the words of the Apostle, the teacher of the Gentiles: "For thus he indicates that the things which belong to one's own discipline and conduct are useful for the merit of a priest, if also those things which are necessary for the knowledge of teaching and holding the faith are not lacking among the rest; because it does not at once belong to a good and useful priest either only to act knowingly [Toledo manuscript: innocently], or only to preach knowingly;
passages.notes: "sacerdoti i merilum" read as "sacerdotii meritum"; "Mei scienliam" read as "fidei scientiam" ("the faith"). The main text's first "scienter" seems to be an error; the Toledo reading "innocenter" (innocently) fits the contrast with the following clause and the context after the passage, and is probably correct. "buic" read as "huic".

passages.original: Attestatur huic [Ms. Tolet., Si aoctrinam vivendo non adjuvet, omnino sibi nihil prosit. Attestatur huic, etc.] libro tuo sanctus Ambrosius in illis libris quos fecit de Officiis. Attestatur sanctus Augustinus dicens : < In actione non amandus est honor in hac vita sine [Ms. Tolet. sive in] potentia, quoniam omnia vana sub sole. Sed opus ipsum, quod per eumdem honorem vel potentiam fit, si recte atque utiliter fit, id est, ut valeat ad eam salutem subditorum quæ secundum Deum est. » Propter quod ait Apostolus : Qui episcopatum desiderat, opus bonum desiderat. Exponere voluit quid sit episcopus, quia nomen est operis, non honoris : Graecum est enim , et inde ductum vocabulum, quod ille qui praeficitur, eis quibus praeficitur superintendit, curam scilicet eorum gerens : episcopus [Ms.
passages.english: To this book of yours [Toledo manuscript: "if he does not support his teaching by his living, it profits him nothing at all. To this bears witness, etc."] Saint Ambrose bears witness in those books which he wrote On Duties. Saint Augustine bears witness, saying: "In action, honour or [Toledo manuscript: or in] power in this life is not to be loved, since all things under the sun are vain. Rather, the work itself which is done through that honour or power [is to be loved], if it is done rightly and usefully, that is, so that it avails for that salvation of those under one's charge which is according to God." On account of this the Apostle says: "Whoever desires the office of bishop desires a good work." He wished to explain what a bishop is, because it is the name of a work, not of an honour. For it is Greek, and the word is derived from the fact that he who is set over [others] oversees those over whom he is set, that is, bearing care for them; for a bishop [Ms.
passages.notes: The main text reads "sine potentia" ("without power"), which does not fit the following "honorem vel potentiam"; the Toledo reading "sive in" ("or in") is translated. The passage breaks off mid-bracket in the middle of a manuscript note; the sentence continues in the following context ("episcopus ... intentio est", Greek episkopos explained as "over-seeing").
